description: The figure contains four separate pie charts intended to show the distribution of answer-refusal categories for four language models on FACTBENCH, with each pie using labeled slices that include counts and percentages and no separate legend. The GPT4-o pie has 2 slices: “Lack of Knowledge” in dark red at 5 (83.3%) and “Safety” in a lighter orange at 1 (16.7%). The Gemini1.5-Pro pie has 5 slices: “Misinformation” in orange at 33 (38.4%), “Lack of Knowledge” in dark blue at 19 (22.1%), “Ethical Advice” in light blue at 14 (16.3%), “Clarification” in pale yellow at 12 (14.0%), and “Safety” in red at 8 (9.3%). The Llama3.1-70B-Instruct pie has 2 slices: “Lack of Knowledge” in orange at 3 (75.0%) and “Clarification” in red at 1 (25.0%). The Llama3.1-405B-Instruct pie has 2 equal slices: “Lack of Knowledge” in orange at 2 (50.0%) and “Misinformation” in red at 2 (50.0%). No slices appear exploded or otherwise visually emphasized, and the slice ordering varies by chart rather than following a consistent descending pattern.
caption_used: The figure presents four pie charts comparing the distribution of answer refusal categories across four language models on FACTBENCH. The 'GPT4-o' chart shows two categories, with 'Lack of Knowledge' accounting for approximately 70% and 'Safety' making up 30%. The 'Gemini1.5-Pro' chart highlights 'Misinformation' as the largest category at 45%, followed by 'Lack of Knowledge' at 20%, 'Ethical Advice' at 15%, and 'Clarification' at 10%, with 'Safety' being the smallest category at 10%. The 'Llama3.1-70B-Instruct' chart indicates 'Lack of Knowledge' as the dominant category at 80%, while 'Clarification' accounts for 20%. Finally, the 'Llama3.1-405B-Instruct' chart shows an equal distribution between 'Misinformation' and 'Lack of Knowledge,' each comprising 50%. These charts provide insights into the varying tendencies of language models to refuse answers based on different categories.
